description: This is a segment from CBS News' 'Face the Nation' featuring an interview between host Margaret Brennan and Shyam Sankar, identified on-screen as CTO of Palantir Technologies Inc. The discussion centers on artificial intelligence policy and public perception. The segment opens with graphics from a CBS News/YouGov voter poll conducted September 16-18, 2026. The first graphic shows 50% of respondents believe AI will 'create more problems than it solves,' 29% believe it will 'solve more problems than it creates,' and 21% don't know. A second graphic shows 45% believe U.S. government policy on AI should 'restrict its use & development,' 28% say 'promote its use & development,' and 27% say 'not take a position.' Sankar argues there should be no guardrails at this moment, stating the burden is on the technology industry to show Americans the benefits of AI in job growth and prosperity. He discusses the concept of an 'unseen force driving the narrative around AI safety,' describing it as a millenarian doomsday cult called effective altruism. He frames the debate as one of control versus monitoring, using an analogy to car safety — noting that while cars have risks, society manages them through liability rather than banning cars. He contends current models are not in control of humans, but humans are in control of them, and that existing laws should be able to handle AI-related harms. description: This is a Tamil-language news explainer video from Puthiyathalaimurai TV's 'PT EXPLAINER' segment. The video uses graphics showing the blue 'M' Muse logo, the Meta branding, and a cute, fuzzy beige mascot character. The presenter explains that Muse functions similarly to ChatGPT and Google Gemini, acting as a personal assistant within Instagram Stories. The video notes that users can access Muse through the story sharing menu, that it has privacy settings, and that it is initially available in select regions like the US and Canada before wider rollout.
